The Graduate School 1
THE GRADUATE SCHOOL
New Mexico State University (NMSU) has a long history of providing
formal graduate study. The ﬁrst master's degree from NMSU was
awarded in 1896. In 1921, the NMSU president appointed a committee to
oversee graduate study. The Graduate School was formally established
in 1956 with a full-time dean, and in the same year, 57 master's degrees
were awarded.
The Graduate School mission is to provide affordable access to high-
quality educational experiences, new modes of graduate education, and
works with dedicated faculty to help students from diverse cultural and
economic backgrounds reach graduate school success. Our vision is to
empower students to succeed and excel while pursuing a meaningful
education. In doing so, we cultivate the collaboration of academic,
professional, and personal skills while helping students graduate in a
timely manner.
Statement of an inclusive environment
NMSU is a proud land-grant institution that is one of the few high-
research universities supporting the state’s population. NMSU’s graduate
students come from an array of lived realities across the world that
reflect rich national and international cultural identities. The Graduate
School is committed to supporting students by ensuring equitable and
inclusive practices that create opportunities for their success and their
ability to thrive.
Policies
Since graduate degrees are awarded for attainment in scholarship, the
requirements stated in this catalog are to be considered as minimal.
The major department or the dean of the graduate school may make
additional requirements as deemed necessary for each candidate.
Responsibility for securing approval of the proposed degree plan
rests with the student and is subject to the approval of the respective
department head or program director. Frequent consultation with the
advisor is essential to satisfactory progress toward degree completion.
Graduate Degree Programs
For a full listing of the Graduate Programs offered at New Mexico State
